articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Defender flaw. AI is apparently better at finding vulns than humans now, which is either progress or the beginning of the end.

articles.title: Stealer Backdoor Found in 3 Node-IPC Versions Targeting Developer Secrets
articles.summary: Cisco's SD-WAN Controller gets pwned with a perfect 10.0 CVSS auth bypass that's already being exploited in the wild. Someone's having a very bad day in San Jose.

articles.title: Microsoft BitLocker-protected drives can now be opened with just some files on a USB stick — YellowKey zero-day exploit demonstrates an apparent backdoor
articles.summary: BitLocker gets absolutely demolished by YellowKey and GreenPlasma zero-days with public PoCs. Your 'encrypted' drives are now as secure as leaving the keys in your car.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets ransomwared nationwide, turning homework submissions into ransom demands. Cybercriminals proving they really will attack anything, even your kid's algebra assignments.

articles.title: Checkbox Assessments Aren't Fit to Measure Risk
articles.summary: Foxconn gets hit by Nitrogen ransomware as part of 600 manufacturing attacks this year. Turns out making iPhones and tolerating downtime don't mix well with ransomware economics.

articles.title: Your Data Was Leaked. Here's What Hackers Hope You Don't Do Next
articles.summary: OpenLoop Health admits to leaking 716,000 people's data in January, because telehealth wasn't dystopian enough already. Your medical records, now with extra cybercrime seasoning.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature, breaking years-old promises about privacy. Meta proves once again that surveillance capitalism trumps user protection.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory lap time: Apple finally enables end-to-end encryption for RCS between iPhone and Android. Only took them forever, but cross-platform encrypted messaging is finally real.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud after SMS phishing sprees. Another young talent learns that social engineering skills don't include avoiding federal prosecution.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: PAN-OS RCE, Mythos cURL Bug, AI Tokenizer Attacks, and 10+ Stories
articles.summary: Malicious node-ipc packages caught stealing developer secrets, because supply chain attacks are the new black. Open source trust model meets reality in the worst possible way.
